title: Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden called out, like a sign that reveals
overview:
Chapter 19 explains how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*: from its *Malchus* comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. The relationship is *gilui ha'helem*, the revelation of what is hidden, and it holds wherever a *yesh* of one world becomes the *ayin* of the next. Unlike *etzem v'hispashtus*, where something actually comes off the essence, here nothing is given: the essence is there, and a sign reveals it, as movement reveals life, words reveal thought and color reveals a ripe apple.

Rabbi Walters builds it on a person. An essential kindness shows itself through the wills it gives birth to, a separate will for each situation, by the associations of a self-image made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will is never wanted for itself: bring the pizza and he never wanted to drive. So the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called lights, drawn off like Moshe's spirit onto the elders, and only the outer letters of each level, as the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's will, become the *Keser* of the next. *Kore hadoros meirosh*: the whole of history is called out of *Adam Kadmon*.

terms.gloss: revelation of what is hidden: nothing is given, the essence is there and a sign reveals it; the relationship of every yesh to the ayin below it
an essence and its spreading forth: something actually comes off the essence, like the energy of a throw or the sun's photons
the hidden sefiros: said plainly, the ten sefiros of Adam Kadmon
He calls the generations from the beginning: Adam Kadmon holds the picture of all history, and each generation is called out in its time
radiance: the light of an essence, which only reveals it
a sign: a thing not essentially connected to what it shows, but always associated with it
the essence of the attribute: the bias that gives birth to particular wills and is not separate from the person
a will for a will: the association in Adam Kadmon that ties a particular will to the essential will
subduing: making yourself do what you do not feel like doing, the naaseh that comes first
transforming: changing the way you look at a thing so that the feeling itself changes
the crowns: the Kesarim of the sefiros of Atzilus are revealed wills, compared to the hidden will of Adam Kadmon

sections.title: From Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden sefiros come out, like a flame from a coal
sections.summary: After the *igulim* and the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, the chapter explains how the lights of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*. Each world first defines what is wanted, then a picture of it, then how to do it; and the relationship between *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*, as between any *yesh* and the *ayin* below it, is *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

phrases.he: (יט) ומעתה יש להבין בשרש עשר ספירות הנאצלים, ששרשם מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בשער הכללים דמבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דעתיק יומין כו'

blocks.text:
Now we have to understand the root of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation): the *Etz Chaim* writes that *Malchus* (kingship) of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* (crown) of *Atik Yomin*.

After the *igulim* (circles) and *yosher* (straight line) of *Adam Kadmon*, the lights of *Atzilus* come out of it. Every world has its *igulim*, then a *yosher*, its *guf* (body), and out of that body the light breaks through into the next world, down to *Asiya* (Action): each time abstract again, but more defined.

blocks.title: From a desire for a home to a house
blocks.text:
First a person has a desire for a home, which is just to feel a certain way. That becomes a desire for a house, already concrete: he defines what a house is, and from that the building blocks he wants, a kitchen, a place that keeps him warm.

Then he pictures a dream house, his wildest dream but something he could in theory have. Then he works out what is practical now, while still working toward the higher one, and how to get it, cutting it down until he knows what to do right now. Each time it goes abstract, then needs a concrete form, and each time it is cut down.

In general there are three stages, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (the three lower worlds), once in the *ratzon* (will) and again in action: three to figure out what you want, three to figure out how to get it. The *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) in the will, down to the end of *Atzilus*, is figuring out what you want.

blocks.title: The house in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya
blocks.text: The general *mashal* (analogy) for *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* is a person making a house. In *Beriya* he plans doors and windows, this room and that, the abstract definition of a house. In *Yetzira* he pictures them: wood, stone or brick, and what shape. In *Asiya* he figures out how to build that form.

Until modern times they could not build very large rooms; the materials were not strong enough. Then came the dome, pillars and other methods, and now steel I-beams: two parallel pieces of metal joined in the middle like an uppercase I, which, unlike a solid block, does not sag under its own weight. Innovations like these let them actually build it; sometimes an architect draws a fine design the construction crew can hardly make.
But your will needs the same three stages. In *Adam Kadmon*, say you want to be happy: first you must ask who you are, and what needs a person like you must fill to be happy.

blocks.title: Morality in schools
blocks.text: A government works this way too: first it settles the basics, life and liberty. He was thinking of this because he had heard a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe complained that in the name of liberty schools teach children no morality, because of the separation of church and state. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.

sensitivity.reason: Reports the Rebbe's complaint that, because of the separation of church and state, schools teach no morality: a stand on an American political dispute.
sensitivity.publishable: A government works this way too: first it settles the basics, life and liberty. He was thinking of this because he had heard a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe spoke about teaching children morality in schools. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The church-and-state line is the Rebbe's own public stand on moral education, reported from a sicha, not Rabbi Walters' politics; weigh whether a reader takes it as Torah or as an American political dispute.

blocks.text: Change the definition on a higher level and everything below changes with it: change *Adam Kadmon*, and you react to the same information in a totally different way. You can only build from the foundation.

So a government that ignores religion is impossible: it sets no ultimate goal, and without one there is no standard to measure decisions on. It takes time, but eventually it breaks down. Even with a separation of church and state, everybody has to agree on common goals the government will uphold, some utopian state it is trying to achieve. Without an ultimate goal you cannot judge anything, because you do not know where you are going: when a dispute comes up, there is no way to decide.

sensitivity.reason: Says a government that ignores religion will break down: a political opinion on church and state.
sensitivity.publishable: Without an ultimate goal there is no standard to measure decisions on. It takes time, but eventually it breaks down. Any group has to agree on common goals, some state it is trying to achieve. Without an ultimate goal you cannot judge anything, because you do not know where you are going: when a dispute comes up, there is no way to decide.

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בענין עשר ספירות הגנוזות בהעלם,
איך שיוצאים לידי גלוי
phrases.en: How they come, how they're revealed.

phrases.he: שזהו מה שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש,
phrases.en: It says that *Hashem* calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history,

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: *Hashem* calls out from *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: Now, how it goes from *Adam Kadmon* to *Atzilus*. The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are the *sefiros hagenuzos* (the hidden sefiros); those before the *tzimtzum* are hidden in the Essence, but *genuzos* plain means *Adam Kadmon*'s. **How they come, how they're revealed** is the relationship called *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

The *hishtalshelus* has two general relationships: *gilui ha'helem*, and *etzem v'hispashtus*, an essence and its spreading forth. Here it is *gilui ha'helem*, and not only between *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*: wherever you go from a *yesh* (something) to an *ayin* (nothing), from an *etzem* to an *or* (light), from the *yesh* of one world to the *ayin* below it, it is *gilui ha'helem*.

That is *kore hadoros meirosh* (He calls the generations from the beginning), from the *rosh* (head) of *Adam Kadmon*: **Hashem calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history**. *Adam Kadmon* is the whole picture of everything that will happen, and each generation *Hashem* calls out to come down to the world.

phrases.he: ואמר בספר יצירה
שזהו כשלהבת הקשורה בגחלת,
phrases.en: that this is like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא יש דמיונות רבים
phrases.en: there's many other types of examples for this thing.

blocks.title: The flame hidden in the coal
blocks.text: The *Sefer Yetzira* (the Book of Formation) says it is **like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal**: hidden, and when you blow on it, it comes out *b'gilui* (revealed), because the coal really is on fire. **There's many other types of examples for this thing**: it was there, and now it comes out.

sections.title: Revealing the hidden is not spreading forth: the sign, not the thing
sections.summary: In *etzem v'hispashtus* something actually comes off the essence, like a thrown stone's energy or the sun's photons. In *gilui ha'helem* nothing is given: the essence is there, and the better the vessel, the more of it shows, as movement shows life and words show thought, a sign with no essential connection to what it reveals.

phrases.he: ויובן יותר מי' כחות הנפש
phrases.en: but we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.

phrases.he: דהנה ידוע ענין העלם וגלוי אינו כהתפשטות כח מן העצם,
phrases.en: That *helem* and *gilui* are not the same as *hispashtus* from an *etzem*.

phrases.he: כמו כח הפועל שמתפשט בפעולה,
phrases.en: like when you throw something.

phrases.he: שזהו מהות כח העצם שנקרא עילה ועלול
אלא כמו בחינת זיו ואור של העצם
phrases.en: but rather it's like the *ziv* and the *or* of the *etzem*,

phrases.he: כהארת זיו אור השמש, וכחיות אור הנפש בכלי הגוף, וכהתחכמות מכח השכל וכהאי גוונא
והיותר דמיון אמיתי לגלוי ההעלם הוא כמו גלוי התנועה מן החי
phrases.en: is like the *gilui hatenua min hachai*: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.

phrases.he: וכאותיות המחשבה ואותיות הדיבור
phrases.en: like when you talk, your *osios hadibur* reveal what you're thinking.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: **But we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.** **Helem and gilui are not the same as hispashtus from an etzem**, as the doer's power goes into the deed **when you throw something** and you spend energy: that is *ila v'alul* (cause and effect).

**But rather it's like the ziv and the or of the etzem** (its radiance and light): the sun's shining, the soul's life in the body, the insight of the intellect; and, truer still, movement revealing a living thing, and the letters of thought and speech.

Really everything has both *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui ha'helem*. Earlier he gave four *meshalim* for *etzem v'hispashtus*: the sun's light, a candle's light, the soul in the body, and throwing. A throw spends energy, a candle burns something up, and the sun's light is a *yesh* coming out of it.
*Gilui ha'helem* means you are given nothing: the *etzem* is there, and how much you can appreciate of it is how much you see.

blocks.title: Exercise and the stronger body
blocks.text: The body's *chayus* (life) has both. Exercising, a person spends energy on what he throws: *etzem v'hispashtus*. But afterwards he is stronger, because his body has become a better, more refined vessel for his soul. The soul's abilities are the same; the body can now be *megaleh* (reveal) more of them.

blocks.title: Light in the room, the sun through the window
blocks.text: The same in sunlight. The light that comes off the sun and just lights your room is *etzem v'hispashtus*, light seen as itself, apart from the sun. Look through the window and the light disappears: you see the sun, its form, and the light only reveals what is there. That is *gilui ha'helem*. Both are going on.

blocks.title: The eye and the ear
blocks.text: The same with the soul in the body. Consciousness goes into the eye, which lets the simple soul reveal only sight, and the ear only hearing. A healthier vessel gets more light, not because the soul gives more, but because it receives better, is more transparent to it: *gilui ha'helem*.

Or the insight of the intellect. A teacher only helps you look the right way at what is already there, and studying sets you up to perceive. That is why the baby is taught the whole Torah before birth: the *koach hamaskil* (power of insight) perceives the whole truth. What you do not see is how it applies here; for that you need *iyun* (close analysis), and the more you refine your brain, the more comes in.

The photons that leave the sun are an actual *hispashtus*: the sun loses something. That is a physical *shefa* (flow), not really *or*. But photons take any form, bouncing off whatever they hit, and hitting your eye they show you the thing: *gilui ha'helem*. What *Chassidus* calls *or* is not physical light but the revealing of the thing.

*Gilui ha'helem* is his main subject here, and these are *meshalim* for it; its main idea comes soon. Some serve for *etzem v'hispashtus* too: one aspect of light or of the soul is a *mashal* for one, another for the other.

He spoke of this earlier, and it is explained at length in the *maamar* (discourse) *Sachar Oscha* in the *Siddur*, on which Reb Hillel bases his commentary here, and, he thinks, in a number of *maamarim* early in *Ayin Beis* (the Rebbe Rashab's series), from *Imrei Bina*'s explanation of the difference.

More particularly there is *etzem v'hispashtus* in the *ruchni* (spiritual) and the *gashmi* (physical), *gilui ha'helem*, *hislabshus* (enclothing). *Chassidus* distinguishes them because different parts of the *hishtalshelus* correspond to them, and the whole needs all of them.

blocks.title: Even a vulture knows
blocks.text: A truer likeness of *gilui ha'helem* **is like the gilui hatenua min hachai: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.** You do not see the life, but even a vulture knows that one who stops moving is dead. Wire something up and shock it and it moves without being alive: movement is just a *siman* (sign) of life.

blocks.title: Go three blocks and make a left
blocks.text: And the letters of thought and speech: **like when you talk, your osios hadibur reveal what you're thinking.** The sounds are not the thought. Told "Go three blocks and make a left at the light," you see the route at once, though all you got was sounds; in another language you would have no idea, because sounds have no essential connection to what they reveal.

phrases.he: וכל זה יותר אמיתי מדמיון שלהבת הקשורה בהעלם בגחלת
phrases.en: And all of these are a better *mashal* than the fire that's inside the coal.

phrases.he: שאף על פי שבגחלת היה השלהבת בהעלם,
phrases.en: even though in the coal the fire was hidden,

phrases.he: אבל הרי על כל פנים ממהות חום שבגחלת יצא השלהבת,
phrases.en: but the coal's actually on fire,

phrases.he: ואין זה אמיתית ענין הגלוי
רק כמו בחינת מראה וגוון לבד,
phrases.en: The real *inyan* of a *gilui* from a *helem* means like an appearance or like a color,

phrases.he: כגוון התפוח
phrases.en: like an apple.

phrases.he: שאינו ממהות התפוח,
phrases.en: The color is not the actual *mahus hatapuach*.

phrases.he: וכידוע

blocks.text: **And all of these are a better mashal than the fire that's inside the coal**: **even though in the coal the fire was hidden** and blowing reveals it, **the coal's actually on fire**, a hot burning, and the flame is the gas it releases, heated and ionized until it gives off light. There is a direct connection.

So in a way the flame is *etzem v'hispashtus* of the fire. That it gives off light only tells you something is burning, "when there's smoke there's fire"; the light is not the burning. That is the *gilui ha'helem* part. Rust is the same burning very slowly, an explosion the same very fast; fast enough, it makes a flame and light.

blocks.title: The color of the apple
blocks.text:
And this is not the true meaning of a *gilui*. **The real inyan of a gilui from a helem means like an appearance or like a color**, **like an apple**. Red outside tells you it is ripe, green that it is not; cut it open, white means sweet and brown means spoiling. But the color is not the ripeness or the sweetness: paint a rotten apple white and it will not taste good.

**The color is not the actual mahus hatapuach** (what the apple is in itself). G-d made apples look like this when ripe and like that when not; they are not essentially connected, but since *Hashem* made them go together, one is a sure *siman* of the other.

sections.title: The attribute shows through the will it gives birth to
sections.summary: A person's essential kindness or cruelty is hidden; it is revealed by the wills and opinions it always produces. The source of those wills, the bias itself, is still the essence, but each particular will is only a sign, like movement revealing life, and a single deed cannot be judged without the whole picture.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בגלוי העלם עצם כחות הנפש,
phrases.en: Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו כח מדת החסד בעצם
שגלוי שלו היינו כאשר מצד עצמיות מדה זו בעצם הנפש, הרי מתהווה רצון ושכל של חסד וטוב תמיד
ולהיפך במי שמדתו העצמית באכזריות,
phrases.en: somebody that's cruel,

phrases.he: מתהווה רצון ושכל לדין ועונש

blocks.text: **Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed** (the essence of the soul and its powers), as with kindness: when this attribute stirs in the soul, a will and an intellect for kindness always come into being. How do people know someone is a nice guy? Because he always wants to do nice things, and whenever he is asked his opinion, he leans towards *chesed* (kindness).
So too when people call somebody a liberal. How do they know what he is inside? Because whenever a question comes up, he leans towards *chesed*, or whatever that side is.

sensitivity.reason: Uses a political label (a liberal) as the example of a person who leans toward kindness.
sensitivity.publishable: So too when people call somebody soft-hearted. How do they know what he is inside? Because whenever a question comes up, he leans towards *chesed*, or whatever that side is.

blocks.text: And the opposite, **somebody that's cruel**. Hitler, may his name be erased, is called a monster. How do we know what he was inside? From what he always wanted, how he looked at things, what he said. That is only a *gilui*: it reveals a personality you cannot see. An essentially cruel person always shows it as a bias, his will and *sechel* (intellect) leaning towards judging, punishing, cruelty.

phrases.he: והנה התהוות מקור לרצון זה, לחסד או לדין, נחשב עדיין מעצם המדה,
phrases.en: the fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence,

phrases.he: שאינו נבדל הימנה כלל

blocks.text: **The fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence**, not separate from it at all: the source of all his particular desires, for kindness or for judgement, is part of who he is, his inner *ratzon*.

phrases.he: אבל מה שנולד רצון בגלוי לדין או להיפוכו,
זהו רק כמו בחינת התגלות מראה לעצם
phrases.en: This is only like a color that's revealing the essence.

phrases.he: כהתגלות התנועה בעצם החי
phrases.en: like the movement that shows that something's alive.

phrases.he: וכגלוי החיות בדבר נבדל, שהוא הגוף
phrases.en: the *gilui hachayus* means the consciousness.

phrases.he: שמפני שהוא חי בעצם,
phrases.en: since the soul is essentially alive,

phrases.he: מגלה חיותו בתנועה
phrases.en: it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body.

phrases.he: וכן מפני שהוא דבר חי בעצם,
phrases.en: and since the soul essentially has a consciousness,

phrases.he: מחיה גם לגוף הדומם
phrases.en: it also has physical perception when it's in the body,

phrases.he: שנקרא חיי בשר כו'
phrases.en: which is called physical life.

blocks.text: But the particular will that is born revealed **is only like a color that's revealing the essence**, like movement revealing life. A person's actions show where his sympathies lie; watch him in different situations and you work out his priorities and personality. "It's impossible really for a person to hide himself": what he wants comes through in how he reacts.

blocks.title: The man tied to a bench
blocks.text: Yet you cannot judge somebody from one deed without the big picture. Tell me a man tied somebody to a bench and cut him up: nice guy or mean guy? There is not enough information. The act itself is not a sure sign, and to think it must mean one thing is wrong.

That leads to a lot of judging people and unnecessary hatred. A person knows what an act would mean coming from his own background, culture and motives; for someone else you need the bigger picture first. Like a word: even knowing its definition, without context and tone of voice you will not necessarily know what it means.

A person could even do what the Torah calls a sin while expressing a real desire to connect to G-d, if he was misled: a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive, raised without Torah) told this is how to connect to G-d expresses a good thing the wrong way, like someone using a word wrongly, whose meaning you get from the context.

That is *gilui ha'helem* in general: something not essentially connected, once associated, reveals the essence. The bias, always looking to *chesed*, is from the essence; the particular deeds are not. So a person can do outwardly *gevura'dik* (stern) things out of *chesed*.

Educating a child, a parent or teacher must often be strict, outwardly the opposite of what they want. But as the Rebbe Rashab says in *Chinuch Lanaar*, if you consistently mean the child's best he will sense it and respond; if not, he will notice that too, and will not listen.

A main problem is a double standard: the child is told something is good, and the parents do not do it, however well they mean. As they say, parents who tell their kids not to do what they did have kids who tell their kids the same. When guests come and the kids must give things up, are the parents teaching what they themselves do, or sparing themselves by making the kids do it? Then the kids resent it. If they see the parents do it, they appreciate it and learn kindness.

The next class reads it again: the born will only reveals the essence, **like the movement that shows that something's alive**. Movement is not life: make something move and it is not alive. But what is alive will move.

blocks.title: Is the baby blind or deaf?
blocks.text: And life revealed in a separate thing, the body: **the gilui hachayus means the consciousness**. You know a person has a conscious soul when his eyes follow you. How do they know a baby is blind or deaf? Clap by its ear, pour water near its eye, wave something before its face, and see whether it responds. The physical responses show whether it has a spiritual consciousness of those things.

**Since the soul is essentially alive**, **it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body**; **since the soul essentially has a consciousness**, **it also has physical perception when it's in the body**, **which is called physical life.**

phrases.he: כי גלוי רצון זה בא בדבר נבדל, שהוא ענין זה של חסד או דין
אבל מקור המוליד רצון זה
הוא בא מכח עצם המדה לבד
phrases.en: it only comes from *etzem hamidda*

blocks.text: For the will comes out in a separate thing. That the soul can move, control and perceive is from its essence; whether this shows in the body is not. So too the will that comes out **only comes from *etzem hamidda*** (the essence of the attribute), but is not *etzem hamidda* itself.

sections.title: One source, many wills: the born will is not what you really want
sections.summary: One essential attribute gives birth to a separate will for each situation, through the associations made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will was never wanted for itself: take away its connection and it vanishes, which is why the world is *yesh me'ayin*, and why prayer must lead the animal soul back to what it really wants.

phrases.he: ומובן ממילא, בהיות שיש כמה אופני דברים שיוליד רצון מיוחד לכל אחד ממקור אחד,
phrases.en: And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*.

phrases.he: שהוא תלוי בעצם המדה תמיד כו'
וגם שכל המטה תמיד כלפי רצון וחסד, היינו רק מצד עצם מדת החסד
phrases.en: the fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature

phrases.he: שמוליד תמיד רצון ושכל לחסד דוקא
ויש כמה ענינים נבדלים
phrases.en: but there are many different things that this will be expressed,

phrases.he: ולכל אחד מוליד רצון ושכל בפני עצמו כו'
phrases.en: and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.

phrases.he: ודי למבין

blocks.text: **And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*** (source), the essence of the attribute. An essentially nice person wants many different things, as each situation calls for, sometimes in a way you would call *gevura* (restraint), like a surgeon.

An intellect that always leans towards kindness comes from the essence of kindness: **the fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature**, and his constant particular wills are a sign of it. **But there are many different things that this will be expressed**, **and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.**

This is what *Adam Kadmon* does: it connects the essential *middos*, its *igulim*, with the particular wills of *Atzilus*, which are not the essential will. A will to cut somebody is particular; whether it is *chesed* or *din* (judgement) depends on how it is associated. That association is made in *Adam Kadmon*: a person forms a self-image and worldview, so he knows how his desire for *chesed*, or for *gevura*, comes out in each situation.

blocks.title: Hunger becomes a desire to eat
blocks.text: The same physically. Once the soul is in the body, its desire to express itself freely there becomes tied to eating and drinking. The wish to stop the stomach's pain becomes a desire to eat, since you learn that eating takes the pain away and gives strength. That desire is created, not essential; but once associated, the one reveals the other: *gilui ha'helem*.

phrases.he: ומובן על כל פנים שיש הפרש גדול בין גלוי הרצון לחסד, שאינו רק בחינת גלוי ההעלם של עצם הרצון, המוליד רצון זה
phrases.en: So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon*.

phrases.he: שהוא בא מכח עצם המדה, שהוא אינו בחינת נבדל כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon***, which comes from the essence of the attribute and is not separate. The will that comes out is detached from your essence: you do not really want it. The essential will you do.

blocks.title: I never wanted to drive
blocks.text: A hungry man has a whole plan: put his shoes on, drive out, get pizza. Someone walks in with pizza, and he starts taking his shoes off. Asked about his plan to drive to the store, he says he never wanted it at all.

That is the meaning of the world being created *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing): its external things are not really what G-d wants. Nothing has to stop the hungry man wanting to drive; he wanted it only because it was tied to what he did want. Take the connection away and the desire vanishes, because it never had its own *metzius* (existence).

That is the point of *davenen* (praying): to show your *nefesh habehamis* (animal soul) that what it really wants, traced back to its essential desire, needs connecting to G-d. Most people are not conscious of this. A person ties what he wants to a certain form and gets stuck in it; when it fails he is disappointed, forgetting it was never what he really wanted.

This can happen because a person really can choose what to want: with *bechira* (free choice) he can make a *prat* (detail) his essential goal, though it is not his inner essence. Once he has a *kavana* (intention), he ranks his inner and external wills.

With people's problems you always do both, *naaseh* and *nishma* ("we will do" and "we will understand"). Having people rethink from scratch what they want is *is'hapcha* (transforming the feeling itself). That is the real meaning of *moach shalit al halev*, the mind rules the heart: change what you associate a thing with and your feeling about it changes, because the feeling is a born will that comes from your essential will through your *sechel*, which makes the associations.

Until he can do that, he starts with *iskafya* (forcing oneself against the feeling), which has its own *maala* (advantage): *Pada b'shalom nafshi mikrav li*. If the whole thing were to see the truth and be a *tzaddik* (righteous man), *Hashem* could have made us *tzaddikim*; He also wants *avoda*, work. So at every level there is something we do not enjoy and an *iskafya* to do. Making yourself do what you do not feel like doing, to connect to G-d, is meaningful because you are giving something up.

That is the *naaseh*, and the willingness to push is what makes the *nishma* possible. So first he resolves on the outward things *halacha* asks: a nice place, standing properly, looking in the *Siddur*, not talking during *davenen*, not taking his *tefillin* off early, finishing *Tehillim* first, whatever shows it is a priority even when he does not feel like it. Then he must start to understand and appreciate what goes on in *davenen*.

sections.title: Atzilus called out from Adam Kadmon: lights, Moshe's spirit, the Kesarim
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are only what was hidden in *Adam Kadmon* coming out, so they are called lights, like the spirit drawn off Moshe onto the elders without his losing any. Their *Kesarim* are revealed wills, like the will to give a poor man a dollar, which *Adam Kadmon* ties to the essential will.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל זה יובן ענין קורא הדורות מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
כמשל הקורא דבר שיצא מהעלמו לגלוי לחוץ
כך כל עיקר בחינת עשר ספירות דאצילות הוא שיצאו מהעלמם לגלוי בלבד
phrases.en: the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui*.

phrases.he: ועל כן נקראו בשם אורות או ספירות,
phrases.en: That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros*,

phrases.he: כמו זיו ואור

blocks.text: This *mashal* explains *kore hadoros meirosh* of *Adam Kadmon*: calling something out of hiding, like telling a man behind a curtain to come out. So **the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui***.

Once *Hashem* had the essential wills for the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), the *igul* of *Adam Kadmon*, He made in *Adam Kadmon* the general picture of what fulfils them. When a situation comes up, the particular will, the Torah and *mitzvos* for it, comes *mimeila* (by itself): the association was already made in *Adam Kadmon*, and the situation only reveals it.

**That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros***, radiance and light: only a revelation of the *etzem*. *Adam Kadmon* is like the *Maor* (source of light), and *Atzilus* is *Hashem* revealing Himself as creating a world.

Say the *chesed* of *Arich* is the light of the *chesed* of *Atzilus*: everything *Hashem* creates He recreates every moment, because He is the true *metzius* and everything depends on Him. That constant recreation reveals the essential thing, decided in *Adam Kadmon*: to reveal Himself as a creator, and not just a creator but essentially one.

Being essentially a creator means everything depends on Him totally. That our world is created every moment reveals it; it is not the G-dliness itself but a symptom, telling you the world's relation to its Creator, and so something about the Creator.

phrases.he: וכמו כל בחינת גלוי ההעלם שאינו רק בבחינת אור, וכבחינת מראה וגוון,
וכמו תנועת החי כו'
phrases.en: like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive.

phrases.he: והיינו כמו ויאצל מן הרוח,
phrases.en: this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*.

phrases.he: שאין זה רוחו של משה
phrases.en: this is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach*,

phrases.he: רק בחינת גלוי אורו וזיוו לבד, הוא שנאצל והופרש, כגלוי שלהבת מן הגחלת וכהאי גוונא כו'

blocks.text: Revealing the hidden is only like light and color, **like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive**. Hence the name *Atzilus*, from *vayatzel min haruach*: **this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*** (elders). **This is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach***: only his light was drawn off, like a flame from a coal, or Rashi's candle that lights others and loses nothing.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's shluchim
blocks.text: When the Rebbe sends out *shluchim* (emissaries), they carry a little of his *ruach*, his ideology. The more *batel* (nullified) they are to his will, the more they succeed, because the Rebbe sees far better than we do and knows what everything is for. You do not have to become Moshe: nullify yourself to his will and you reveal his *ruach*.

blocks.title: A conduit for G-d's wisdom
blocks.text: So with a person who learns Torah. It is G-d's wisdom, not his, but if he works to understand just what G-d is saying, people will think him very smart. He has only become a better conduit for it.

So *Hashem* made the elders conduits of Moshe's *ruach*, opening them to see better with a little of his *ruach hakodesh* (holy spirit), his *nevua* (prophecy), so they could know the truth as judges.

phrases.he: וכל זה יובן על פי משל הנזכר לעיל מענין גלוי הרצון בדבר נבדל
phrases.en: So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*,

phrases.he: שיוצא מהעלם עצם הרצון שמצד עצמיות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character.

phrases.he: כך בחינת כתרים דעשר ספירות דאצילות הן רק בחינת גלוי רצון לגבי העלם עצם הרצון שנקרא רצון לרצון,
שהוא בבחינת אדם קדמון כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*** **which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character**. The *Kesarim* (crowns) of *Atzilus* are only a revealed will beside the hidden *ratzon l'ratzon* (will for a will). The will of *Atzilus* is particular, like giving a poor man a dollar; the *ratzon l'ratzon* in *Adam Kadmon* is the bias that counts it as nice and so ties it to the will for *chesed*, and to the *ratzon kadum* (preceding will), the *igulim* before *Adam Kadmon*.

So if a person wants *chesed*, and *Adam Kadmon* tells him this is connected, he will want this. So *Hashem*'s decision to want a *dira b'tachtonim* in a certain order makes the Torah, whose *chachma* (wisdom) is *batel* to *Adam Kadmon*: it tells you accurately, in each situation, what brings you closer to the *dira* and what farther.

Had *Hashem* wanted the *dira* another way, the revealed will would change by itself. Some things He said will not change, and that is why they cannot. But essentially it is not that putting on *tefillin* is good and not putting them on bad: *Hashem* decided He wants it, so now it is connected to G-d, and so it is good.

phrases.he: וכמו מבחינת העלם הרצון דחסד דאדם קדמון נמשך גלוי רצון לחסד דאצילות שנקרא כתר דחסד כו'
וכן מבחינת העלם רצון דחכמה כו'
phrases.en: from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: As the hidden will for *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon* draws out the revealed will for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, the *Keser* of *chesed*, so *Hashem*'s decision to be a creator became a will to create our world, only one instance of it. What reveals the *etzem*, that He is a creator, is that He creates it every moment.

And so with *chachma*: **from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus***. Wanting to be revealed as wise, He willed wisdom in the world and the Torah, and we see a lot of wisdom in the world.

sections.title: From Malchus of Adam Kadmon to the Keser of Atzilus: the giver's speech becomes the receiver's will
sections.summary: Only the outer expression, the *Malchus*, of each level becomes the *Keser* of the next: a person's self-image measures each situation, the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's own will, and the teacher's words become the student's understanding. So the external letters of *Adam Kadmon* define *Atik* and *Arich*, and all of history is chosen from what is in *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: אך כמו שמובן ממשל הנזכר לעיל שזהו הנקרא התהוות רצון לרצון,
הרי הוא בא בבחינת הכלל
phrases.en: so it's like a *klal*,

phrases.he: להוליד כמה מיני רצון וכמה ענינים אופנים שונים כו',
phrases.en: and includes many particular things: whatever each circumstance, that inner *etzem ratzon* to be kind will come out in different ways.

phrases.he: כך מבחינת רצון לרצון לחסד באדם קדמון נולד כמה מיני גלוי רצון של חסד באצילות
phrases.en: So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: As is now understood, this is a *ratzon l'ratzon*. *Adam Kadmon* is the general will for everything you will ever do, **so it's like a *klal*** (a general whole) **and includes many particular things**: the inner will to be kind comes out differently in each circumstance. **So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.**

phrases.he: והענין הוא דמבחינת המלכות של מדה דאדם קדמון נעשה בחינת כתר דמדה דאצילות
phrases.en: from the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: ובכללות העשר ספירות הרי רק מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דאצילות
והוא רק מבחינת אותיות וגלוי עצם העלם הרצון, נעשה אור העצם של גלוי רצון כו'
(שהוא כמו שמבואר באות הי''ח
דרק מבחינת סוף מעשה דעצם הרצון נעשה רצון לרצון שהוא עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון)
phrases.en: only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*,

blocks.title: The self-image of a talmid chacham
blocks.text: **From the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus***. The *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is the outward, definable form. Say a person's clear self-image whispers in his ear that he wants to be a *talmid chacham* (Torah scholar); its *Malchus* is the whole *hanhaga* (conduct) of such a person. He measures every situation against that form: what fits, he wants, and what does not, he wants against. That makes the *Keser* of his particular wills, like the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

Only from the letters, the revealing of the hidden essential will, does the revealed will come into being, as section 18 explained: **only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon***, and so only from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes *Keser* of *Atzilus*. Now a *mashal*.

phrases.he: (על דרך דוגמא, מגלוי רצון שבדבור המשפיע נעשה עצם הרצון למקבל
כמו שמאותיות גלוי השכל שבדבור שבמשפיע נעשה עצם אור השכל במקבל
phrases.en: How the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher.

phrases.he: וכך רק מאותיות וגלוי חסד שבדבור דמשפיע נעשה אור הרצון לחסד למקבל
כידוע בכל עילה ועלול,
phrases.en: this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul*,

phrases.he: שמבחינת האחרונה שבעילה נעשה ראש ושרש לעלול
phrases.en: That his *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*.

blocks.title: Your wish is my command
blocks.text: From the will revealed in the speech of the *mashpia* (giver) comes the essential will of the *mekabel* (receiver). The servant tells the king, "Your wish is my command": his will is for the *baal haratzon*, the one whose will it is. How does he know what to want? Whatever the king tells him, the outward revealing of the king's will, becomes his will.

That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): give over the point of your will, and whatever he tells you becomes your full inner will. The thing is not the essential will, but since he said it, it gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*: anyone who tried to stop you, you would die or kill rather than let him.

sensitivity.reason: Says that with mesirus nefesh a servant would kill a person who tried to stop him carrying out the order; out of context it reads as approving violence.
sensitivity.publishable: That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): give over the point of your will, and whatever he tells you becomes your full inner will. The thing is not the essential will, but since he said it, it gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*: nothing anyone did could stop you.

blocks.title: The student and the teacher
blocks.text: So with a teacher: **how the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher**. They want to learn whatever he knows; trusting that he is an expert with something they lack, they accept what he says as true.

To learn properly you must be *batel* and accept, even before you understand, that he knows better, and just try to understand him. Allow that maybe he is wrong, and when it does not make sense you will call it untrue. Knowing that he knows is what guarantees you will understand it.

And so the will for kindness in the receiver comes from kindness revealed in the giver's speech: if you love someone who praises another, you will love that one too, because you trust him. As is known, **this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul***: the last level of the cause becomes the head of the effect. **His *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*** (his outside becomes your inside).

phrases.he: וכך מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון בכלל נעשה בחינת כתר דעתיק יומין כו'
phrases.en: the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: דהיינו מבחינת גלוי רצון לרצון שבדבור בלבד,
נעשה בחינת מקור כל גלוי רצון שמצד התענוג שנקרא כתר דעתיק יומין כו' וכמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: And so from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*: **the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*** (its letters), the *ratzon l'ratzon* revealed in speech. *Hashem* chooses which part comes out now: *kore hadoros meirosh*, He picks the generation, and that choice shapes how all the wills come out.

It becomes the source of every revealed will that comes from the *taanug* (delight), the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. A person enjoys what fulfils his self-image and hates what goes against it. What *ratzon* and *taanug* are comes later, but it is the same with G-d.

phrases.he: והיינו כללות ענין העשר ספירות דאצילות שיצאו מהעלם עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, כמו שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש כו':
phrases.en: That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: This is the whole matter of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, out of the concealment of the ten of *Adam Kadmon*: *kore hadoros meirosh*. **That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.** There *Hashem* chose the essential form in which He wants to reveal Himself in this world.

It is also the form of *Moshiach* and of the *dira b'tachtonim* He chose, and it defines how He runs the world at every moment, by which aspect of *Adam Kadmon* He is revealing now: the whole of history. That is why *nevua* is possible: know the story in *Adam Kadmon* and you know how it will come out.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui ha'helem*, and how do the sunlight in a room and the sun seen through the window show both?
Why are movement, speech and the color of an apple truer *meshalim* for *gilui ha'helem* than the flame hidden in a coal?
How do you know that a person is kind or cruel, and why can a single act, like tying a man to a bench and cutting him, not tell you?
What does the man who takes his shoes back off when the pizza arrives show about the born will, and what does it teach about the world and about *davenen*?
Why are the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* called lights, and what does Moshe's spirit placed on the seventy elders show about them?
How does the servant who says "Your wish is my command" explain that only the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*?

notes.text: Lines 1 and 2 are read at the start of class 66 without a rendering; his next sentences describe the chapter's subject (how the lights of Atzilus come out from Adam Kadmon) rather than translate the lines, so those phrases keep their Hebrew alone. Other phrases he reads without translating: the first half of line 3, the end of line 7, line 9, the end of lines 10 and 12, the end of line 13 ("v'kayadua"), the second half of line 14, lines 15, 22 and the start of 23, the end of line 24 ("shehu talui b'etzem hamidda tamid"), the end of line 25, the end of line 17, the first half of line 18, the end of line 26, line 31, lines 32-33 (for line 33 he gives the curtain mashal, not a rendering), the end of line 35, the start of line 36, line 38, line 41, line 42, the start of line 44, lines 47, 49 and 51, the start of line 48, line 46 (not read), line 54, and the words "v'amar b'Sefer Yetzira" of line 5.
Line 10 is read at 67 w118-134 without a rendering; its phrases cite his second reading of it later in the class, where he translates it (67 w1481-1515 and w1605-1621).

Line 46 is not read aloud. His sentence at 71 w347-369 ("Just like only from Malchus of the igulim becomes Keser of A"K, so too only from Malchus of A"K comes Keser of Atzilus") follows his reading of line 48; its first half is the en of line 48's second phrase. Its second half restates lines 45-46, but since he never reads line 46, line 46's phrase has no en (review change); the sentence is in the explanation block.
Lines 27-29 are not read in any class: class 69 goes from line 26 to a long explanation and then reads line 30. They are kept as a no-recording passage.

The man "tied down to a bench and cut up" (68 w867-955) is not explained in class 68; in class 69 (w497-519, w672-694) he names the surgeon and the will "to cut somebody" as a will that only its association can show to be chesed. The block keeps the riddle as he posed it and the surgeon in the block where he says it; it was not flagged, since the point is the surgeon. A reviewer may want a flag for the image.

Sources as he gives them: the maamar Sachar Oscha in the Siddur, with Reb Hillel's commentary on it; "I think" a number of maamarim at the beginning of Ayin Beis based on Imrei Bina (67 w1315-1373); Chinuch Lanaar, which he first ascribes to the Frierdiker Rebbe and then corrects to the Rebbe Rashab (68 w1373-1428); Rashi's candle on vayatzel (70 w632-663). Kept as said; not checked.

At 69 w1510 he says "Yeah, well, that's the thing. You always have to do both with people, with anytime when people have these kind of problems", as if answering someone; no question is heard on the tape (the series has no audible students). Written as part of the avodah block, not as a question. The block does not quote "Yeah, well, that's the thing" (review change).
